newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UN tribunal postpones third war crimes trial.
newsitem.headline: UN tribunal postpones third war crimes trial.

text.p: The U.N. war crimes tribunal for the former Yugoslavia has postponed the trial of a Croat and three Moslems accused of atrocities at the Celebici detention camp in central Bosnia at the request of their defence lawyers.
"The Celebici trial has been postponed to March 10," a spokeswoman for the Hague-based court said on Monday.
The trial had been scheduled to start on January 28. The postponement was to allow the defence counsel more time to prepare its case, she said.

The accused -- Moslems Zejnil Delalic, Hazim Delic and Esad Landzo, and Croat Zdravko Mucic, are charged with the murder, rape and torture of Bosnian Serb detainees at the camp in 1992. All four men have pleaded not guilty.

Delic and Landzo are accused of beating men to death with wooden planks, baseball bats and shovels, and of torturing detainees, some in their 60s and 70s, with pliers, corrosives, electric currents and hot metal pincers.

Mucic, a former camp commander and Delalic, then a regional commander of Bosnian Moslem forces, are charged with responsibility for the actions of their subordinates. Both are accused of at least 14 murders.
Set up by the U.N security council in May 1993, the tribunal has indicted more than 70 Serbs, Croats and Moslems for alleged war crimes but holds only seven in custody.
Its first trial, of Bosnian Serb Dusan "Dusko" Tadic, finished in November with a verdict expected this spring.

The tribunal has also handed down its first sentence, a 10-year jail term for a young Croat soldier who confessed to taking part in a Serb massacre of Moslems after the fall of the U.N. safe area of Srebrenica.
